top.line: Maps show what to build and where markets exist
top.para: Since 2022 I have said Wardley maps changed how I think, and the site now holds eleven in articles, seven in a vault and five in a talk. A map is a graph with a value chain and an evolution axis, telling you what moves the needle, what to build or buy, and whether a market exists.

in-short.line: A map is a value chain and chosen axis
in-short.para: The two kinds of context, value chain down and evolution across, are what make a map useful, and the evolution axis is a choice. A commoditised layer is a hard sell; custom building on top of one is the market. Maps are stories, they nest, and every figure is now published as data.

what.line: The evolution axis is a chosen scale, not fixed
what.para: A map's vertical axis is a value chain anchored on a user; the horizontal is evolution, using Wardley's genesis, custom built, product and commodity. A 2022 Open Security Summit talk listed eleven shifts, and a lost post proposed risk, data or governance axes. Every dot is a claim; a map you cannot be wrong about is a diagram.

why.line: Maps reveal needle movement, altitude, build or buy, markets
why.para: The weekly uses: seeing what moves the needle, spotting optimisation at the wrong altitude, deciding build or buy by column, asking whether a market exists, finding flow and attrition, naming players and where to hook, giving a common language, starting with the user, drawing many maps, and the peace of no longer carrying things in your head.

best.line: The site's best maps, each with its originating context
best.para: The collection: the mandate stack drawn from outside and inside, the Pay after you read afternoon, the three frames of Agentic cost, Places of highest leverage, A Mac of the agent's own, and the before and after of Every mistake added a rule. Vaults add Strategy Maps' seven maps, ThreatModCon 2025's five, and Agent Desk.

market.line: sgit's market sits above commodities; RiskMandate's layer moved
market.para: Every sgit layer, storage, version control and encryption, is a commodity and a hard sell; the market is the custom building above them, which the vault serves. For RiskMandate, agents became a commodity in the last year, moving the opportunity up to agent behaviour, which is genesis and custom built everywhere.

story.line: Reading one map frame by frame tells a story
story.para: The eight frames of the Pay after you read afternoon are read out: the meter at genesis, going live on Stripe, personas hooking the articles, versions on git, the encrypted share on a vault, the reader card, and dashed next steps. Seven questions, one picture, and a reader learns what the business is.

fractal.line: Every node on a map is itself a map
fractal.para: As in fractal semantic graphs, zooming into a dot makes it the anchor of a child map, placed where the dot sat on the parent's evolution axis. The figure goes three levels down: business, vault, door. It also goes up to the market. Most wrong decisions draw the right map at the wrong altitude.

decks.line: Two printable decks present the maps as slides
decks.para: Two decks on the site print to PDF from the browser, one slide per landscape page with nothing uploaded. Why I love Wardley maps has twelve slides explaining the technique through these maps; Reading one map walks the eight frames of the afternoon with one question per slide.

data.line: Every Wardley map on the site is one query
data.para: Each article's graph at articles/graphs now lists its figures with file, URL, caption, kind and frames, and Wardley maps are tagged. Finding every Wardley map with context is one read of articles/graphs.json and a filter on kind. The same change added play, pause and step controls to animated maps.

community.line: Three ideas offered to the Wardley mapping community
community.para: The maps are source, in Mermaid's Wardley syntax or small scripts, so placements can be disputed line by line. The evolution axis as a choice deserves debate with professional mappers. Nested maps, with the dot as the next anchor, are either known practice not yet written up or an extension worth testing elsewhere.

limits.line: Placements are judgements, and several claims rest on memory
limits.para: Every placement is the author's claim, not a measurement. The eleven shifts are a 2022 list, not the shorter one used now. The alternative-axis post was not found, so it is restated from memory. The market readings can be wrong when layers move, and the fractal anchoring rule is a practice, not a theorem.

sources.line: Sources: a voice memo, the linked articles and vaults
sources.para: Written from a voice memo on 12 October 2026 by the site's agent, with the argument and responsibility the author's. The maps come from the linked articles and three vaults, with only the three-altitude figure and collage new. The 2022 talk was at the Open Security Summit on 14 July 2022; the figure indexing shipped in v0.7.77.
